Header: Bactrocera dorsalis ( Bactrocera invadens ) Amharic: yeferafira zenbe; Tigrigna: fire hamema

Prevention: Remove fruit fly hosts such as neglected citrus, mango, hot and sweet pepper plants
Cover fruits immediately after fruit set with plastic bags to prevent flies from laying eggs on the fruit
Hoe the ground underneath the guava tree canopy to expose pupae to sunlight and predators
Do not use collected damaged fruits to compost as this will increase the infestation
Conserve natural enemies by preventing ants from climbing the guava trees by applying ashes at the base of the tree
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: mango, citrus, peppers
Intensify monitoring during hot weather conditions which are favourable for fruit fly development
Look for brown spots on the skin of fruits during fruit setting
Cut fruits open to look for maggots (white worm the length of a fingernail) in the fruit, leaving a soft rot on the skin of the fruit
As soon as the pest is present consider using the direct control methods
Direct Control: At least twice a week throughout the season remove infested fruits from the tree and the ground and bury them more than 60 cm deep to avoid spread of the pest
Or collect infested fruits in a plastic bag, seal the bag and expose to sun light untill the maggots and flies are dead
Restrictions: There are currently no registered pesticides in
Ethiopia for the management of guava pests
